message.content: The sculpture most frequently cited as the quintessential icon of 19th‑century art is **“The Thinker” by Auguste Rodin**. Although its final bronze version was cast in 1902, the original marble study dates back to 1880–1881, placing its conception squarely in the late 19th century. Rodin’s work captured the era’s fascination with psychological depth and modernist form, and “The Thinker” has become a universal symbol of contemplation and artistic genius.
